name: Mount Everest
hook: The world's highest peak and the handful of stories Jeopardy tells about it.

facts.label: Earth's highest peak
facts.statement: Mount Everest is Earth's highest peak, on the Nepal-China border; Tibetans call it Chomolungma, "Goddess Mother of the World."

facts.label: George Everest
facts.statement: Everest is named for George Everest, a former Surveyor-General of India who objected to the honor.

facts.label: Hillary and Norgay
facts.statement: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay made the first ascent of Everest on May 29, 1953.

facts.label: Edmund Hillary
facts.statement: Hillary was a New Zealand beekeeper who later reached the South Pole by tractor and appears on the country's $5 note.

facts.label: George Mallory
facts.statement: George Mallory answered "Because it's there" when asked why he wanted to climb Everest; he vanished on the mountain in 1924.

facts.label: Into Thin Air
facts.statement: Jon Krakauer's Into Thin Air recounts the 1996 Everest disaster, in which eight climbers died.

facts.label: K2
facts.statement: K2 is the second-highest peak after Everest; Reinhold Messner made the first solo ascent and climbed without bottled oxygen.
